column1: # dx-metrics — identity overrides. Tab-separated. Edit freely; never edit code.
# SENSITIVE: once filled in, this file contains commit author emails and GitHub
# logins. It is operational state, not an export. Do not commit a filled-in copy
# of it, do not paste it into a ticket, and do not use anything derived from it
# to evaluate a person.
# Columns:  directive <TAB> key <TAB> value <TAB> note(optional)
#   email    <commit-email>   <github-login>     confirm an email GitHub could not resolve
#   alias    <other-login>    <canonical-login>  two accounts, one human
#   bot      <login>          <why>              force-classify as a bot / machine
#   human    <login>          <why>              force-classify as a human (beats the regex)
#   exclude  <login>          <why>              a real account that is not a person (shared/service)
#   name     <login>          <Display Name>     canonical name for the .mailmap
# The `email` key may be a GLOB (* and ?). Machine addresses come in families —
# a new devbox mints a new hostname — so a glob keeps the file correct when the
# box is replaced. Later lines win, so put globs first and exceptions after.
# Overrides are applied AFTER the automatic rules, so a line here always wins.
# WHY THIS FILE MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS
# Every address left unmapped becomes an execution with an UNKNOWN STEERER. That
# is honest, and it is also the number that gates the whole report: above ~10%,
# no attribution-derived trend on the dashboard is presentable. Filling this in
# is the single highest-leverage thing an operator can do to a run.
# Two different fixes live here and they must not be confused:
#   * a HUMAN committing from a machine  -> map the address to that human's login
#     (a person on their own laptop is still that person steering; the agent is
#     the executor)
#   * a MACHINE with no identifiable human behind it -> map it to a
#     dxm-machine-* login. Anything matching ^dxm-machine- is auto-flagged as a
#     bot by schema.sql, so it is excluded from delivery metrics rather than
#     silently inflating the human population.
# EXAMPLE MAPPINGS — replace these with your own
# Everything below is illustrative. The shapes are real (they are the shapes
# that actually occur), the addresses are not. Delete what does not apply and
# add your own.
# CONFIRM BEFORE YOU ADD A LINE. Every mapping should be checked against the
# commit author NAME recorded in git for that address, not guessed from the
# local part of the email. A wrong line here is a permanent, silent
# misattribution — worse than the gap it closes.
# An in-house coding agent running on ephemeral devboxes. The git author name
# on these typically reads "CI Agent" / "CI Agent Operator" / "Build Bot".
email
column4: in-house agent devbox; no human steerer identifiable

# The residual unknown-steerer population is usually real humans whose commit
# email GitHub cannot resolve to an account — contractors on an agency domain,
# people who left, addresses never added to a GitHub profile. Guessing a login

# STEERER and are reported as one.
